design:
Steady means the verdict does not depend on how busy the machine is. It does not mean the test got weaker, so every change to a guard test is paired with proof that the guard still fires when the defect it guards is introduced (FR on still-catching).

Load, for this document, means every logical CPU kept busy by a load generator the acceptance drive starts, for the whole measurement. It is a fixed, repeatable stand-in for 'the operator is gaming and two agents run suites'.

The steady set is a named list in the repository, one test id per line with the record that put it there (a Fix flaky test task, a wall-clock assert, or membership of the never-freezes family). The drive reads it, so the list and the measurement cannot drift apart.

Proposed numbers, to be confirmed by the operator: 10 repetitions under load, 0 failures; migration family at most 40% of its baseline test-seconds.

problem:
Since 2026-11-05 this project's hub-tests check runs at landing only (operator's settings change, read back mode=ro). So what is left of the check cost is landing batches held by tests that fail for reasons outside the work:
- 19 'Fix flaky test' tasks were filed between 2026-10-28 and 2026-11-04. test_turn_starts_never_freeze_the_hub.py::test_a_turn_start_that_creates_its_checkout_never_stalls_the_loop was 'fixed' four times (10-31, 11-02, 11-03 twice) and still fails under load.
- On 2026-11-04 one test failing on master showed in 15 check runs, including the runs of the tasks written to fix it.
- The never-freezes family decides from a loop-lag probe with a 100 ms limit (hub/tests/_loop_lag.py:30). Its own notes record 110-196 ms pauses with no CPU spent when a busy machine preempts the thread holding the GIL (F1119), which is a stall the code under test did not cause.
- Six more tests compare elapsed real time against a fixed limit (listed under evidence).
- The migration family (test_migrations.py and test_migration_*.py, 170 tests) took 580 test-seconds, 154 s wall at -n 4, measured 2026-11-05 in the Architect worktree. That is about 9% of a full suite's ~6,600 test-seconds. Its slowest tests are downgrade/upgrade round trips at 9-12 s each, each building its database from nothing.

requirements.rationale: The drive measures from this list, so the list is the definition of 'steady' and cannot drift from what is measured.
requirements.statement: The repository holds a list of the steady set: every test in the never-freezes family, every test named by a 'Fix flaky test' task filed from 2026-10-28 to 2026-11-04, and the six wall-clock assertions named under evidence. Each entry gives its test id and the record that put it there.

requirements.rationale: Today these tests fail under load for reasons the work did not cause, and each failure holds a landing batch.
requirements.statement: Every test in the steady set passes 10 consecutive repetitions while every logical CPU is kept busy for the whole run, with 0 failures, and also passes 10 consecutive repetitions on an otherwise idle machine.

requirements.rationale: A guard made steady by making it unable to fail is worse than a flaky one: it reports safety that is not there.
requirements.statement: For each never-freezes test, when a blocking call of at least 250 ms is placed on the Hub's event loop in the path that test guards, the test fails on every one of 10 repetitions, idle and under load.

None of the six wall-clock assertions named under evidence fails because the machine is slow: each is rewritten so its verdict does not depend on how long real work takes, or it stays, with a comment beside it saying why load cannot move the time it measures, and passes the under-load repetitions.

No test in the steady set is deleted, skipped, marked expected-to-fail or retried to make it pass. A test merged into another is listed in the change's evidence beside the test that now catches what it caught.

requirements.rationale: Non-goal: product fixes. The test's job is to report a real stall.
requirements.statement: When a steady-set test fails under load because the Hub code it guards really does block the loop or hold a lock, the test is left failing and a finding naming the code path is recorded in scripts/drive/FINDINGS.md, rather than the test being changed to pass.

requirements.rationale: Measured 2026-11-05: 580 test-seconds, 154 s wall at -n 4, about 9% of a full suite.
requirements.statement: The migration family takes at most 40% of its baseline test-seconds (sum of setup, call and teardown durations), with the baseline and the new figure measured by the same command, on the same machine, in the same session.
Every migration revision whose upgrade or downgrade the family exercises today is still exercised, and a downgrade deliberately broken in one revision still fails at least one migration test.
The full Hub suite's total test-seconds on an idle machine is lower after the change than before, measured the same way.

in_scope: The never-freezes-the-hub family: the tests built on hub/tests/_loop_lag.py, and the slow-share, main-watch and no-write-lock-across-git tests
The tests the gate filed Fix flaky test tasks for since 2026-10-28, and the six wall-clock assertions found by reading
The migration test family: hub/tests/test_migrations.py and hub/tests/test_migration_*.py
An acceptance drive that repeats the steady set under load and reports each failing test
non_goals: Changing Hub product code. If a test is flaky because the Hub really does stall under load, that is recorded as a finding, not hidden by the test
Deleting a test, marking it skip or xfail, or adding retries, to make it pass
Tiered or change-sized test selection, and idle-time runs: slice 4
Changing the project's check settings, the suite entry point or its one-at-a-time lock: slice 3
Speeding up tests outside the migration family

summary: Slice 5 of 'Checks cost less on a machine that is in use', for this repository only, taken ahead of slice 4 (tiered tests) at the operator's agreement on 2026-11-05. The Hub tests that fail when the machine is busy, the never-freezes-the-hub family and the tests the gate has filed 'Fix flaky test' tasks for, pass on a loaded machine and still fail when the freeze they guard against is really there. The migration tests take well under half their current time while exercising every migration they exercise today.
